sources.title: Interview-note image transcription containing the linked-list big-integer addition problem
Structured source record for linked-list big-integer addition
Deterministic Java validation against java.math.BigInteger and input-immutability checks

claims.text: The preserved source asks to add two big integers represented by linked lists, with the most-significant digit at the head and the ones digit at the tail, return a new result list, and discuss time and space complexity; it does not specify null handling, leading-zero normalization, or permission to mutate inputs.

Because the list traversal direction is most-significant to least-significant while decimal carry propagates from least-significant to most-significant, two stacks expose the next unprocessed low-order digits without mutating the source lists; prepending each result digit restores the required most-significant-first list order.

The exact Java implementation passes eight fixed cases and 5000 deterministic randomized cases up to 80 digits against java.math.BigInteger, while also verifying that both input lists remain unchanged and that null/invalid-digit implementation contracts fail fast.
The implementation pushes each of m+n source digits once and pops each at most once, so it runs in O(m+n) time and uses O(m+n) auxiliary stack space in addition to the output list.

findings: The candidate stays within the recovered source contract and explicitly labels null, leading-zero, digit-range, and input-mutation behavior as implementation choices rather than source facts.
The two-stack design directly resolves the mismatch between list traversal direction and carry propagation direction without mutating the inputs.
The carry invariant and head-prepend argument are explicit enough to explain correctness rather than relying only on passing examples.
The executable test uses java.math.BigInteger as a structurally different oracle on 5000 deterministic random cases up to 80 digits, so the validation does not duplicate the candidate algorithm.
The test also detects accidental mutation of either input list and locks down the candidate's fail-fast API boundary.

After the first machine-audit finding, the follow-up section was rewritten into five explicit question-specific 问/答 entries instead of relying on bold bullet formatting that the quality gate could not recognize.
The alternative reverse-list approach is presented as a tradeoff conditioned on permission to mutate input, not as an unconditional improvement.
No project experience, missing sample data, or unstated online-problem constraints are fabricated; required human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
